main_body: Beehive-shaped thatched hut: a large conical straw roof (rows 0-57) over a short clay-brick wall (rows 57-76) with an arched dark doorway and a grey stone plinth
top_band: Light to mid straw-yellow thatch slope, rows ~3-56 down the middle column, drawn as a domed roof surface in banded courses; it ends in a lighter front edge around rows 53-55
evidence: In the middle column the thatch roof reads as a large sloped surface lit from above and as the main top volume. Its lower edge steps to a dark eave shadow (rows ~56-59) over the brown wall, which is a separate vertical face. The doorway is inset, with a dark frame, a lintel and a dark interior. The roof surface is clearly visible, not a thin rim. It is the same roof-over-wall structure as the reference houses, so it counts as 3/4.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 5 straw tones (pale yellow, golden, mid ochre, dark brown, deep brown), with per-course straw ticks and a darker right side for form. The outline is dark brown and follows the material rather than being a black line. The wall has several brown tones with brick dashes and a stone plinth with speckle. The wall and door interior are somewhat flatter and simpler than the reference stone and plaster walls, and the door is a mostly flat dark fill. That makes it slightly thinner than the reference, though it would sit acceptably beside it.
